selectionEvidence.collectionIdentity: The Met accession 64.228.21 is a Moche Portrait Head Bottle, dated to the 5th–6th century.
selectionEvidence.availability: On view at The Met Fifth Avenue, Gallery 362, as checked 2026-07-24.
selectionEvidence.imageStrategy: Official Met IIIF object image; Public Domain.
selectionEvidence.importanceCandidate: A candidate important work for showing the Moche portrait-head and stirrup-spout ceramic tradition through a documented, currently on-view example.
selectionEvidence.nearestComparators: Two related vessels are in Chicago’s Field Museum (100076) and Lima’s Museo Nacional de Antropología, Arqueología, e Historia.
selectionEvidence.decisiveDifference: The related vessels differ in their headband designs.
selectionEvidence.independentCollectionLine: Part of The Met’s Arts of the Ancient Americas holdings in the Michael C. Rockefeller Wing.

structureSummary.coreValue: A modeled and painted Moche portrait-head bottle makes the relationship between repeatable molds, individualized painted detail, and uncertain ritual or mortuary meanings concrete.
structureSummary.mediumPeriod: Ceramic, slip, pigment; 5th–6th century, Moche, Peru.
structureSummary.routeRole: A focused stop for Andean ceramics and Moche visual culture.
